prompts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity desktop screenshot concept for CloudX Hardware Manager, a local developer workbench plugin. Wide 16:10 screen, sharp readable English text, flat front-on product UI, no perspective or desk objects. Match CloudX: near-black charcoal background, subtle gray cards and borders, restrained amber-yellow active buttons and tab, thin cyan outer pane edge, compact developer-workbench typography, Lucide-like line icons. Top global bar: CLOUDX and window controls. One amber workspace tab HARDWARE. Plugin header Hardware with subtitle Shared lab inventory. Horizontal navigation Inventory, Reservations, Tags & types, Statuses & hooks. No marketing illustrations, no artificial 3D effects. All data is illustrative. Show Inventory active. Header right Add hardware button. Search field Find hardware, filters Type: SSH + UART, Tags: arm64 and deploy, Availability: Available, Clear filters. Main content 60% width inventory table with columns Hardware, Type, Tags, Up, Free to use, Reservation. Rows: web-01 SSH arm64/deploy Up Yes Available; lab-02 SSH x86_64/build Up Yes Reserved: Codex / kernel test; board-03 UART arm64/uart Unknown No Needs attention. Label Up and Free to use as custom statuses, reservation independently. Show small summary 3 hardware / 1 available / 1 reserved / 1 needs attention. Selected web-01 opens 40% detail pane with heading web-01, SSH, 10.0.0.24:22, username lab. Tabs Overview / Notes / Activity. Overview shows tags arm64 deploy, status Up (command, checked 12 s ago), Free to use Yes (manual). Reservation Available. Clearly visible Notes for agents card: Use /srv/validation. Do not reboot this machine. Notes are guidance. Show Edit and Reserve hardware amber button, purpose input Deployment validation. Bottom compact help Skills available to Codex, Claude and Forge workers. Detailed data table and practical clear hierarchy. Preserve all named functions in readable controls.

Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity desktop screenshot concept for CloudX Hardware Manager, a local developer workbench plugin. Show Inventory active and an Edit hardware page for web-01, with a clear Back to inventory link. Two-column form, detailed readable fields. Left Basics: Name web-01; Type SSH dropdown, available types SSH and UART; Physical resource group lab-server-01 (SSH and UART entries for one machine share this group); Description ARM64 validation server; capability tags arm64, deploy and Add tag; large Notes for agents editor containing Username: lab. Use /srv/validation. Do not reboot this machine. No per-command approval is required after reservation. Right SSH connection settings: Host 10.0.0.24, Port 22, Username lab; Authentication: SSH agent, Identity file alternative; Known hosts file /home/lab/.ssh/known_hosts; Host key checking Required. Small SSH status No connection opened while editing. Below right editable Custom statuses cards Up command and Free to use manual Yes, link Configure statuses and hooks. Bottom section Reservation setup with optional Before reserve script link, optional On release script link. Bottom pinned Cancel and Save hardware buttons. Add a compact note Private keys stay on the host. Only references are saved. Include Delete hardware secondary menu. No invented permissions or marketing features.

Show a saved UART hardware item board-03 in a two-column detailed screen, navigation Inventory active. Heading board-03 / UART with Edit and Back to inventory. Left saved connection settings card: Device /dev/serial/by-id/usb-Lab_board_03; Baud 115200; Data bits 8; Parity None; Stop bits 1; Flow control None. Physical resource group board-03. Capability tags arm64, uart, firmware. Notes for agents card: Console login: lab. Do not toggle DTR. Use raw byte I/O; a serial console is not an SSH shell. Custom statuses Up: Unknown, Free to use: Yes (manual). Right active UART access panel with amber Reserved by you / Firmware validation banner and duration 04:12. Session transcript on dark monospace terminal: [00:01] RX board-03 login: / [00:04] TX lab / [00:05] RX Password: / [00:09] RX lab@board-03:~$. Label illustrative test data, no real secret. Below receive pane Read window 2000 ms, Max bytes 4096 and Read button. Transmit area with Text / Base64 tabs, input uname -a, Line ending LF, Send bytes button. Bottom Session open and Release hardware button. Separate collapsed Serial control lines section with explicit Set lines action and no automatic DTR toggle. Small note Owner only. Reads and writes require the active reservation. Do not show fake command exit codes for UART.

Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity desktop screenshot concept for CloudX Hardware Manager, a local developer workbench plugin. Wide 16:10 screen, sharp readable English text, flat front-on product UI, no perspective or desk objects. Match CloudX: near-black charcoal background, subtle gray cards and borders, restrained amber-yellow active buttons and tab, thin cyan outer pane edge, compact developer-workbench typography, Lucide-like line icons. Top global bar: CLOUDX and window controls. One amber workspace tab HARDWARE. Plugin header Hardware with subtitle Shared lab inventory. Horizontal navigation Inventory, Reservations, Tags & types, Statuses & hooks. No marketing illustrations, no artificial 3D effects. All data is illustrative. Show Statuses & hooks active for selected hardware web-01. A header selector Hardware: web-01. Split content 55% left Custom statuses and 45% right Reservation hooks. Left row Up with source Command, Boolean result, Current true, checked 12 s ago. Selected status edit form Label Up; Value type Boolean; Source Bash command; host-side bash editor: printf 'true\n'; Result contract stdout is one JSON value; zero exit required. Timeout 5 s, max age 60 s, Schedule 30 s dropdown. Required to reserve toggle ON and Required value true. Refresh status button. Second row Free to use source Manual, current Yes with a Yes/No toggle; Required to reserve ON. Add status control with Boolean / Text / Enum choices. Note Reservation state remains separate. Right Before reserve optional enabled Bash editor: ./prepare-lab.sh ; Working directory /srv/lab-hooks ; Deadline 30 s ; Context via JSON stdin. On release optional Bash editor: ./cleanup-lab.sh ; Working directory /srv/lab-hooks ; Deadline 30 s. Readable callout Claim is saved before Before reserve runs. Hook failure keeps hardware held for review. Bottom recent run area Before reserve: succeeded, exit 0, duration 1.2 s, View log. Footer Save configuration and Cancel. A small footnote Scheduled checks pause while another owner holds the resource. Avoid any Run hook button that bypasses reservation. These scripts are illustrative config.

Horizontal navigation Inventory, Reservations, Tags & types, Statuses & hooks. No marketing illustrations, no artificial 3D effects. All data is illustrative. Show Reservations active. A compact table with columns Hardware / Owner / Purpose / State / Held since / Owner observed / Actions. Rows web-01 Codex tab kernel-fix / deployment validation / Active / 10:32 / 5 s ago; board-03 Forge worker W-42 attempt A-3 / firmware check / Preparing /10:40/3 s ago; lab-02 Claude tab boot-debug / serial recovery / Recovery required /10:17/Unknown. Show Open owner and Details actions. Banner Heartbeats show activity. They do not expire reservations. Selected lab-02 detail below or right: owner exact tab and execution, reservation R-103 generation 7, hook outcome unknown, notes Do not reboot, reason Owner termination unconfirmed. A modal titled Force release lab-02 shows Expected reservation R-103 / generation 7; Reason input Device checked manually; explanation Revoke old access and stop CloudX-managed operations. Remote jobs may remain. Separate acknowledgement checkbox I accept unresolved external activity; Cancel and Force release buttons. Keep destructive action visually distinct in red. Smaller history panel shows reserve, owner lost, recovery required timestamps with per-operation logs. Clearly differentiate Release own reservation from Force release. No automatic TTL countdown or assumed remote kill.

Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity desktop screenshot concept for CloudX Hardware Manager, a local developer workbench plugin. Wide 16:10 screen, sharp readable English text, flat front-on product UI, no perspective or desk objects. Horizontal navigation Inventory, Reservations, Tags & types, Statuses & hooks. No marketing illustrations, no artificial 3D effects. All data is illustrative. Show Tags & types active. A two-column catalog management page. Left Capability tags table with Tag / Description / Hardware count / Actions. Rows arm64 / 64-bit ARM / 2 / Edit, x86_64 / x86 build host /1/Edit, deploy / Deploy target /1/Edit, uart / Serial console /1/Edit, firmware / Firmware tests /1/Edit. New tag button. Small selected tag edit card label deploy, description Deploy target, Save tag and Delete tag. Note Used tags need reassignment before deletion. Under tags an Agent discovery card: List tags; Filter using all / any / exclude; IDs stay stable when labels change. Right Hardware types table with Type / Owner / API / State / Operations. SSH / hardware / v1 / Ready / exec, upload, download. UART / hardware / v1 / Ready / read, write, set lines. PCIe / future provider / — / Planned / Not installed. Readable note Types are registered in code. No UI code upload. Selected SSH type detail Config schema v1, host, port, username, auth reference; Typed input and output schemas; Provider cannot grant reservations. Small physical resource groups table lab-server-01 / web-01 SSH and console-01 UART / shared reservation, board-03 / board-03 UART / one reservation. Show Add group and Edit group controls. Bottom footer All AI tabs can discover tags, types and available hardware. Compact, implementation-oriented, no invented online marketplace.

Horizontal navigation Inventory, Reservations, Tags & types, Statuses & hooks. No marketing illustrations, no artificial 3D effects. All data is illustrative. Show Inventory active, saved item web-01 / SSH with Back to inventory and Edit. Execute script is active, and a small file transfer drawer at right makes transfer capabilities visible. Main editor Remote Bash script contains uname -m then printf 'validation ready\n'. Fields Deadline 60 s and Output limit 64 KiB; Run script amber action. Result pane from an illustrative completed earlier run shows Exit code 0, duration 0.3 s, stdout aarch64 and validation ready. Note Regular files only. Path policy applies. Bottom mini history has access opened, script completed, and upload completed with request IDs. Footer Connection owned by this reservation; Close access and Release hardware buttons distinct. Include a small muted Unknown transport outcomes keep hardware held message. All controls practical and readable; no fake live connection claim.

edits.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this CloudX hardware UI concept. Preserve all layout, controls, typography, colors, content and dimensions except the small subtitle directly under Serial control lines at bottom right. Replace that subtitle verbatim with: Set RTS / DTR only. Opening may reset the board. This corrects a technical error: CTS and DSR are inputs and cannot be set. Do not change the notes card or other text. Keep opaque dark background.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this CloudX Hardware Tags & types UI concept. Preserve layout, all main controls, fonts, colors and dimensions.
